\begin{definition}[Fourier sparsity]
\lean{FABL.fourierSparsity}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p087-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p091-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p276-b009
}
\label{FABL.fourierSparsity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierSupport}
For a function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, its Fourier sparsity is the cardinality of
its Fourier support.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier expansion on the Boolean cube]
\lean{FABL.fourier_expansion_support}
\label{FABL.fourier_expansion_support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierSupport, FABL.fourier_expansion, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let
$x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. For each subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, define its monomial by
$\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ and its Fourier coefficient by $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb
E_y[f(y)\chi_S(y)]$, where the expectation is uniform over the cube. Then
$f(x)=\sum_{S:\,\widehat f(S)\ne0}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parseval identity on Fourier support]
\lean{FABL.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_support}
\label{FABL.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierSupport, FABL.parseval, FABL.uniformInner}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let its Fourier support be the collection of subsets
with nonzero Fourier coefficient. The sum of the squared Fourier coefficients over this
support equals the uniform average of $f(x)^2$ over the sign cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise bound by Fourier sparsity]
\lean{FABL.sq_le_fourierSparsity_mul_secondMoment}
\label{FABL.sq_le_fourierSparsity_mul_secondMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierSparsity, FABL.fourierSupport, FABL.fourier_expansion_support, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_sq, FABL.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_support}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $x$ be a
point of the sign cube. The square of $f(x)$ is at most the Fourier sparsity of $f$
times the uniform average of $f(y)^2$ over the sign cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moment bound by Fourier sparsity]
\lean{FABL.fourthMoment_le_fourierSparsity_mul_secondMoment_sq}
\label{FABL.fourthMoment_le_fourierSparsity_mul_secondMoment_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierSparsity, FABL.sq_le_fourierSparsity_mul_secondMoment}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. Write $\widehat
f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i]$ for its Fourier coefficient at
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $s$ be the number of subsets $S$ for which $\widehat
f(S)\ne0$. Then $\mathbb E_x[f(x)^4]\le s\bigl(\mathbb E_x[f(x)^2]\bigr)^2$, where the
expectations are uniform over the cube.
\end{theorem}
